simple: Userdata is one of Luau's basic types. It is used for data that actually lives inside the Roblox engine, which is written in the languages C and C++. You will not usually make userdata yourself. Most beginners only need to know the name, so it does not confuse them when they see it.
analogy: Userdata is like a sealed box delivered from the factory. You can use the buttons on the outside, but the parts inside were built somewhere else, in a different language.
keyPoints: Userdata is one of the basic types in Luau.
It stands for data that comes from C or C++ code, the languages the Roblox engine is built with.
You use userdata through the functions and properties it offers, not by looking inside it.
Roblox objects such as Parts are userdata under the hood: `type(workspace)` gives "userdata", while `typeof(workspace)` gives the more exact "Instance".
The page points to the Lua manual for more detail.

terms.userdata: A Luau type for values that are really made and stored by the engine's C/C++ code.
terms.C/C++: Programming languages used to build big, fast programs like the Roblox engine itself.
terms.arbitrary: Any kind at all. Arbitrary data means it could be any sort of information.
terms.basic type: One of the built-in kinds of values in Luau, like number, string, boolean, table, nil, and userdata.

watchOut: Worrying about userdata too early. You can build lots of games without ever needing to think about it.
